title: Start here: NInfer RTX 4090 installation and first local API request
body:
Welcome! This is the independently maintained RTX 4090 / SM89-focused NInfer-all project.

The current stable Windows release is [v0.1.4](https://github.com/spk-c/ninfer-all-rtx4090/releases/tag/rtx4090-v0.1.4). The exact downloaded archive passed a real-model RTX 4090 smoke test (32K context, DFlash2 K=5, two correct short requests); [verification scope](https://github.com/spk-c/ninfer-all-rtx4090/blob/master/docs/releases/rtx4090-v0.1.4-gpu-verification.md).

### Getting started
1. Download every archive volume and its SHA-256 manifest from [Releases](https://github.com/spk-c/ninfer-all-rtx4090/releases/latest). Verify and extract with 7-Zip, keeping all backend directories intact.
2. Install a compatible NVIDIA driver and the Microsoft Visual C++ runtime. A separate CUDA Toolkit is not required for the portable package.
3. Download a native .ninfer model using the [model catalog](https://spk-c.github.io/ninfer-all-rtx4090/models.html).
4. Generate the correct launch command using the [VRAM and launch planner](https://spk-c.github.io/ninfer-all-rtx4090/configurator.html). Start at 32K context, one sequence, localhost. For the Huihui non-Swift artifact, use rk4v4 and DFlash2 K=5 as a conservative starting point.
5. Check the API:
```powershell
Invoke-RestMethod http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/models
```
Use the returned model ID in your client. If the server requires no authentication, keep it bound to localhost.

Optional: [checksum-verified installer and GUI launcher](https://github.com/spk-c/ninfer-all-rtx4090/blob/master/docs/rtx4090-windows-setup.md). The installer was tested using the cached release archive; the GUI argument validator passed, but interactive desktop testing remains open.

[English guide](https://spk-c.github.io/ninfer-all-rtx4090/windows.html) · [Deutsche Anleitung](https://spk-c.github.io/ninfer-all-rtx4090/windows-de.html) · [Troubleshooting](https://spk-c.github.io/ninfer-all-rtx4090/troubleshooting.html)

If you're stuck, share your exact release, GPU, model filename, start command and relevant error (remove keys and private prompts). Upstream developers and component authors deserve credit; see the repository notices.

title: Model selection: Huihui Qwen 27B vs Swift 1.5 and Bonsai 2.5
body:
Which model should you try on a 24 GiB RTX 4090?

| Native artifact | File size | Packaged backends | Evidence |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| [Huihui IQ3_S, no Swift](https://huggingface.co/SPK1337/Huihui-Qwen3.8-27B-Uncensored-GSQ-RCO-IQ3S-Vision-DFlash2-MTP-NInfer) | 13.99 GiB | DFlash2, MTP; optional vision | 1,831 historical serving requests; v0.1.4 real-model smoke test |
| [Huihui Swift 1.5 IQ3_S](https://huggingface.co/SPK1337/Huihui-Qwen3.8-27B-Swift1.5-Abliterated-IQ3S-DFlash2-NInfer) | 13.99 GiB | DFlash2, MTP; optional vision | 63/63 historical HTTP requests; 2,048-token decode observations at 32K and 160K input |
| [Bonsai 2.5 PTQ1_0](https://huggingface.co/WaveCut/Ternary-Bonsai-2.5-27B-PTQ1_0-NInfer-v3) | 6.17 GiB | MTP | v0.1.4 short Engine benchmark |
| [Bonsai 2.5 PQ2_0](https://huggingface.co/WaveCut/Ternary-Bonsai-2.5-27B-PQ2_0-NInfer-v3) | 7.37 GiB | MTP | v0.1.4 short Engine benchmark |

File sizes are not resident VRAM. DFlash2 and MTP are alternatives, not simultaneous backends. Vision must be enabled separately on compatible artifacts and was not verified in these text benchmarks. Bonsai 2.5 is a different quantized model family variant, and the measurements do not establish comparative quality.

The two Huihui benchmarks were recorded under different workloads and builds, so the numbers cannot rank the models. Pick based on your task and measure quality, memory and throughput yourself.

[Model catalog](https://spk-c.github.io/ninfer-all-rtx4090/models.html) · [VRAM planner](https://spk-c.github.io/ninfer-all-rtx4090/configurator.html) · [Bonsai guide](https://spk-c.github.io/ninfer-all-rtx4090/bonsai.html)

What model and context are you using? Include exact artifact, backend, and workload if sharing results.

title: RTX 4090 benchmark thread: v0.1.4 DFlash2, MTP and Bonsai 2.5 results
body:
Here are the first short Engine measurements from the exact published v0.1.4 Windows binary, on one RTX 4090.

Huihui IQ3_S: 2,048 prompt tokens, 128 timed decode tokens, 32K capacity, rk4v4, GDN FP16, 2 measured repetitions and one warmup, n-gram copy disabled.

| Backend | Decode tok/s |
| --- | ---: |
| No speculation | 70.38 |
| MTP K3 | 200.31 |
| MTP K5 | 242.59 |
| DFlash2 K3 | 201.93 |
| DFlash2 K5 | 257.13 |
| DFlash2 K7 | 326.41 |
| DFlash2 K9 | 269.33 |

K7 was fastest on this particular short fixed corpus, not necessarily coding or long-context prompts. No global default change is implied.

Bonsai 2.5 MTP K3 with default n-gram copy width 15: PTQ1_0 291.69 decode tok/s and 4,635.36 prefill tok/s; PQ2_0 323.88 decode tok/s and 6,295.90 prefill tok/s. This separate test differs in model and n-gram settings.

A limited no-speculation HTTP pilot used 6 requests per engine and 128 output tokens: NInfer 68.58 vs llama.cpp 59.85 output tok/s including request wall time. All six output strings differed; BF16 vs F16 KV, non-interleaved run order and conversion differences limit the comparison. No vLLM result or general engine ranking is claimed.

[Full Engine methodology](https://github.com/spk-c/ninfer-all-rtx4090/blob/master/docs/performance/rtx4090-v014-bonsai-and-draft-2026-11-26.md) · [HTTP pilot](https://github.com/spk-c/ninfer-all-rtx4090/blob/master/docs/performance/rtx4090-v014-llama-cpp-pilot-2026-11-26.md) · [JSON dataset](https://spk-c.github.io/ninfer-all-rtx4090/benchmarks-data.json)

### Contribute a reproducible result
Please include release/commit, model and hash, GPU and driver, context, prompt/output token counts, speculation and cache flags, warmups and repetitions, TTFT/prefill/decode (label which), memory, output checks and failures. Negative results are welcome. Avoid publishing private prompts. Use the same workload and cache state when comparing engines.

title: Long-context coding agents: configuration, memory and troubleshooting
body:
For a local coding client, start with a single sequence and 32K context before increasing it. The [command generator](https://spk-c.github.io/ninfer-all-rtx4090/configurator.html) can produce model-specific Windows commands. Use the OpenAI-compatible base URL http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1 and the model ID returned by /v1/models. Tool calling and reasoning settings depend on your client and artifact.

### When increasing context
- Count rendered input, output and media tokens together. Keep space for the reply.
- KV capacity is shared between concurrent sequences; file size is not VRAM use. Account for weights, drafter, workspaces, recurrent state, desktop and reserve.
- Compare rk4v4/rk8v4 and DFlash2/MTP individually. Keep the same prompts and sampling, and check output quality.
- Prefix caching may help repeated coding sessions, but do not report cached prompt time as fresh prefill.
- If allocation fails, reduce context/concurrency or disable optional vision/drafting. Record the original error.

Historical Swift 1.5 measurements at approximately 32K and 160K input reported 229.04 and 191.78 client-observed decode tok/s for 2,048 output tokens; these are single observations, not v0.1.4 qualification or general throughput.

[Long-context guide](https://spk-c.github.io/ninfer-all-rtx4090/long-context.html) · [VRAM guide](https://spk-c.github.io/ninfer-all-rtx4090/vram.html) · [Serving reference](https://github.com/spk-c/ninfer-all-rtx4090/blob/master/docs/serving.md) · [Swift benchmark report](https://huggingface.co/SPK1337/Huihui-Qwen3.8-27B-Swift1.5-Abliterated-IQ3S-DFlash2-NInfer/blob/main/BENCHMARK.md)

Share what you use for coding: model, client, context size, typical output length, time to first token, repeated-prefix behavior and any quality or stability issues. Please redact secrets and private code.
